record.title: A Lean-formalized search target for the open unforced Navier–Stokes problem
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint defines a positive energy defect for a periodic-cube, unforced Leray–Hopf solution at fixed viscosity and reports a Lean 4 formal reduction: the defect is equivalent to a uniform positive lower bound on time-averaged energy flux through all sufficiently fine dyadic Fourier shells. The paper gives necessary admissibility conditions and argues that finite Galerkin computation cannot witness the required uniform ceiling; its 12 pseudo-spectral runs at 128³ and 256³ meet a temporal flux condition but fail to sustain the floor toward the Kolmogorov scale. This is a bounded mathematical search specification, not an unforced singularity result. The authors state that their Lean library contains no Navier–Stokes object and does not connect the reduction to a separately formalized Leray–Hopf theory; the target remains open.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For an unforced Leray–Hopf solution on the periodic three-dimensional torus at fixed viscosity, the paper states that positive energy defect over a time window is equivalent to an eventually uniform positive lower bound on time-integrated flux through dyadic Fourier shells.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report Lean 4/Mathlib formal proofs of the reduction and related necessary conditions. They explicitly state that the library contains no Navier–Stokes object and does not connect the reduction to a formalized Leray–Hopf theory.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports 12 pseudo-spectral runs at resolutions 128³ and 256³. The runs approach the temporal flux-floor condition but lose the common floor toward the Kolmogorov scale; the authors state that these finite floating-point diagnostics establish nothing about a true solution.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper states that the unforced positive-defect problem remains open and that the forced Navier–Stokes and forced/inviscid Euler constructions it discusses are outside the target class.

evidence_gaps.description: The linked current Lean package and its exact theorem/import scope have not been built or independently audited; the paper identifies Lean 4.33.0 and Mathlib 4.33.0 but says the library contains no Navier–Stokes object.
No formal derivation connects the abstract sequence/function hypotheses used by the reduction to an actual unforced Leray–Hopf solution of Navier–Stokes.
The authors' finite-resolution flux diagnostics have not been independently reproduced; they do not establish the uniform fine-scale floor in any case.

brief.importance_rationale: If the paper's formal reduction and search criteria are sound and useful, they provide a concrete way to target computational work on a major open regularity problem. This is notable methodological progress, while the actual unforced positive-defect solution remains open and the formal bridge to Navier–Stokes objects is absent.
limitations: The paper does not construct an unforced Navier–Stokes singularity or solve the positive-defect problem, which it states remains open.
The Lean library contains no Navier–Stokes object; the bridge from the abstract sequence/function theorem to formalized Leray–Hopf objects is explicitly undone.
The 12 pseudo-spectral runs are finite floating-point diagnostics and cannot establish the uniform condition at arbitrarily fine scales or witness a positive defect.
the research desk did not build the linked current Lean package, independently audit the proof, or reproduce the simulations.
The necessary conditions in the paper are not sufficient conditions for a positive defect.
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint defines a positive energy defect for a periodic-cube, unforced Leray–Hopf solution at fixed viscosity and reports a Lean 4 formal reduction: the defect is equivalent to a uniform positive lower bound on time-averaged energy flux through all sufficiently fine dyadic Fourier shells. The paper gives necessary admissibility conditions and argues that finite Galerkin computation cannot witness the required uniform ceiling; its 12 pseudo-spectral runs at 128³ and 256³ meet a temporal flux condition but fail to sustain the floor toward the Kolmogorov scale. This is a bounded mathematical search specification, not an unforced singularity result. The authors state that their Lean library contains no Navier–Stokes object and does not connect the reduction to a separately formalized Leray–Hopf theory; the target remains open.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report the shell-balance reduction, a set of necessary conditions for a candidate positive defect, and 12 pseudo-spectral diagnostic runs at 128³/256³. They report the time condition is nearly met but the fine-scale condition fails approaching the Kolmogorov scale.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint, its date and its stated scope and limitations are directly inspectable. This review re-read the full HTML and linked repository README but did not build the current Lean package, execute the simulations, or independently verify the mathematical argument.
technical.implementation_status: A preprint and linked Lean source repository are public. No current-package build or independent verification was performed in this review.
technical.mechanism: The paper takes the energy defect of an unforced fixed-viscosity Leray–Hopf solution over a time window, derives a shell-truncated energy balance, and identifies the limit of integrated dyadic-shell flux with the defect. A positive defect is then equivalent to a common positive lower bound on the averaged flux for all sufficiently fine shells. The Lean development formalizes the stated implications over abstract real sequences/functions under hypotheses; the paper does not encode a Navier–Stokes solution object.
technical.novelty: A formalized reduction of the positive-defect target to a uniform averaged dyadic-shell flux criterion, together with search admissibility conditions and an explicit account of why finite Galerkin computations cannot establish the required scale-uniform claim.
technical.regime: Unforced incompressible Navier–Stokes on the periodic three-dimensional torus at fixed viscosity, for a Leray–Hopf solution from smooth data. The finite numerical diagnostics use the authors' pseudo-spectral setup at 128³ and 256³; the formalized reduction is over abstract sequences/functions with the Navier–Stokes conditions supplied as hypotheses.
technical.reproducibility: The paper links a Lean 4.33.0/Mathlib 4.33.0 repository and reports 12 spectral runs. The linked current package was not built in this review; the paper says the package is not connected to an existing formalization of Leray–Hopf theory. No independent numerical reproduction was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper contrasts the required scale-uniform flux floor with its own finite-resolution simulations, which approach the time condition but lose flux across finer shells near the Kolmogorov scale. It supplies no independent reproduction or matched computational baseline.

brief.title: A Lean-formalized search target for the open unforced Navier–Stokes problem
brief.why_it_matters: A precise scale-uniform flux target and explicit admissibility criteria can help researchers distinguish useful numerical diagnostics from evidence for an unforced singularity. The contribution concerns how a major open problem might be searched; it does not solve that problem, and the formal bridge to actual Navier–Stokes objects remains absent.
